proof.text: Put $C=L[[Z]]$. Apply [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division] to the finite family $f_{i,0}=\bar f_i$ in $C$: its order, homogeneous forms, diagram and indexed basis hypothesis are exactly the ones assumed here. Denote its supported quotient maps by $Q_i:C\to C$ and remainder by $R:C\to C$. Thus $g=\sum_iQ_i(g)f_{i,0}+R(g)$ uniquely with the prescribed supports. They are $L$-linear, and, writing $\operatorname{ord}_Z(0)=+\infty$, satisfy $\operatorname{ord}_Z Q_i(g)\ge\operatorname{ord}_Z g-d_i$ and $\operatorname{ord}_Z R(g)\ge\operatorname{ord}_Z g$. Negative lower bounds impose no condition. Only the division and order clauses of the cited node are used.

proof.text: By the coefficient-family definition [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], an element of $B$ is equally a family of scalars indexed by $(a,\gamma)\in\mathbf N^m\times\mathbf N^n$. Regroup it as $\sum_a W^a g_a(Z)$ with $g_a\in C$. Multiplication in this notation has coefficient $(gh)_a=\sum_{b\le a}g_bh_{a-b}$: this follows by regrouping the finite decompositions of a fixed pair $(a,\gamma)$. In particular write $f_i=\sum_aW^af_{i,a}$ and $h=\sum_aW^ah_a$. The constraints on $Z$-support hold for a series exactly when they hold for each $W$-coefficient. Every family $(g_a)_a$ defines an element of $B$; no convergence in $Z$ of the family as $a$ varies is required.

proof.text:
Construct $q_{i,a},r_a\in C$ by induction on $|a|$. Once all smaller parameter degrees have been constructed, set
$$e_a=h_a-\sum_i\sum_{0<b\le a}q_{i,a-b}f_{i,b},\qquad q_{i,a}=Q_i(e_a),\quad r_a=R(e_a).$$
The inner sum is finite, and every $a-b$ in it has smaller total degree. For $a=0$ it is empty, so the initial values are $Q_i(h_0),R(h_0)$. The fibre division identity gives $h_a=\sum_i\sum_{b\le a}q_{i,a-b}f_{i,b}+r_a$. Define $q_i=\sum_aW^aq_{i,a}$ and $r=\sum_aW^ar_a$ using Step 2. That coefficient identity for every $a$ proves $h=\sum_iq_if_i+r$. Each coefficient has the required support by Step 1, so the whole series has it. This is a construction by parameter degree, not a claim that a chosen algebraic or regular coefficient lift exists.

proof.text: For uniqueness subtract two supported expressions for the same $h$ and induct on parameter degree. If all lower coefficient differences vanish, the degree-$a$ equation reduces to $0=\sum_i u_{i,a}f_{i,0}+v_a$, since every other summand contains a lower coefficient difference. Fibre uniqueness in [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division] forces $u_{i,a}=v_a=0$. This starts at $a=0$ and proves equality coefficientwise. Adding expressions, or multiplying an expression by any $c\in A$, preserves $Z$-supports (each coefficient outside a support stays zero). Uniqueness therefore proves $A$-linearity of all quotient and remainder maps. Their reductions modulo $(W)$ are $Q_i(h_0),R(h_0)$ by the base case of Step 3. If $v$ is already supported outside $D$, its unique expression is $v=\sum_i0f_i+v$; hence $r(v)=v$ and in particular $r^2=r$.

proof.text:
For continuity assume the vertex family nonempty and put $c=\max_i d_i$, $\lambda=c+1$. Give $W^aZ^\gamma$ weight $\lambda|a|+|\gamma|$. Suppose $h$ has no monomial of weight $<T$. Induct in Step 3 to prove
$$\operatorname{ord}_Z q_{i,a}\ge T-\lambda|a|-d_i,\qquad \operatorname{ord}_Z r_a\ge T-\lambda|a|.$$
Indeed $h_a$ has order at least $T-\lambda|a|$. For $0<b\le a$, the induction bound on $q_{i,a-b}$ and the nonnegative order of $f_{i,b}$ give a product order at least $T-\lambda|a|+\lambda|b|-d_i\ge T-\lambda|a|+1$. The fibre estimates in Step 1 applied to $e_a$ now give the displayed bounds, including when their right sides are negative. Thus $q_i$ has weight at least $T-d_i$ and $r$ weight at least $T$. For a monomial of total degree $u$, its weight lies between $u$ and $\lambda u$. Consequently input of total order at least $T$ gives $q_i$ of total order at least $\max(0,\lceil(T-d_i)/\lambda\rceil)$ and $r$ of total order at least $\lceil T/\lambda\rceil$. These bounds tend to infinity and prove continuity for $(W,Z)$-adic topology. No assertion that $f_i$ has total order $d_i$ is used.

proof.text: Assume now $B/J$ is flat over $A$. We first prove $J\cap\mathfrak nB=\mathfrak nJ$ directly from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-equational-criterion]. If $u\in J\cap\mathfrak nB$, choose $b_j\in B$ with $u=\sum_{j=1}^mW_jb_j$. The images $[b_j]\in B/J$ satisfy $\sum_jW_j[b_j]=0$. Flatness and the cited trivial-relation criterion give finitely many $y_\ell\in B/J$, $a_{j\ell}\in A$ with $[b_j]=\sum_\ell a_{j\ell}y_\ell$ and $\sum_jW_ja_{j\ell}=0$. Choose lifts $t_\ell\in B$. Then $v_j=b_j-\sum_\ell a_{j\ell}t_\ell$ lies in $J$, and $u=\sum_jW_jv_j$ since the other finite sum is zero. This proves the nontrivial inclusion; the converse is immediate from $J$ being an ideal. Neither finite generation of $J$ as an $A$-module nor a Noetherian intersection theorem has been assumed.

proof.text: For $h\in J$, the identity of Step 3 shows $r(h)\in J$. Its reduction is $R(\bar h)$ by Step 4. Here $\bar h\in\bar J$, so the assumed supported expression for every element of $\bar J$, together with fibre uniqueness, gives $R(\bar h)=0$. Thus $r(J)\subseteq J\cap\mathfrak nB=\mathfrak nJ$. For $v=r(h)$ write $v=\sum_jW_jh_j$ with $h_j\in J$ using Step 6. Since $r(v)=v$ and $r$ is $A$-linear, $v=\sum_jW_jr(h_j)\in\mathfrak n r(J)$. Iteration gives $r(J)\subseteq\mathfrak n^kB$ for every $k\ge0$. A series in $\mathfrak n^kB$ has all coefficients of parameter degree $<k$ zero, by finite convolution. Hence $\bigcap_k\mathfrak n^kB=0$ by the coefficient-family definition. Therefore $r(h)=0$ for all $h\in J$, which gives the required supported sums, including $h=Z^\beta f_i\in J$.

proof.text: Let $\varphi:A\to A'=L'[[W']]$ be the given continuous local coefficient homomorphism, and define $\Phi:B\to A'[[Z]]$ by $\Phi(\sum_\gamma a_\gamma Z^\gamma)=\sum_\gamma\varphi(a_\gamma)Z^\gamma$. It preserves sums and products: for a fixed $Z$-exponent the convolution sum is finite, and a ring homomorphism preserves that finite sum. It preserves any $Z$-support restriction because zero coefficients stay zero. Applying $\Phi$ to a whole-series identity therefore gives $\Phi(h)=\sum_i\Phi(q_i)\Phi(f_i)+\Phi(r)$, and in particular preserves all zero-remainder identities. This conclusion needs no claim that the substituted quotient is flat or that the substituted homogeneous family still satisfies the basis hypothesis. Coefficients stay in the completed rings throughout.

proof.text: If the vertex family is empty, then $D=\varnothing$, the sum is empty, and the unique division is $r(h)=h$, with no quotients. It is $A$-linear, continuous and compatible with reduction. Here $J=0$, so the ideal assertion is vacuous. If $m=0$, Step 3 has only parameter exponent $0$ and is exactly the fibre division; $\mathfrak n=0$ makes the intersection and remainder argument immediate. If $n=0$, there is no positive-degree exponent $\alpha_i\in\mathbf N^0$, so the family is empty and the first case applies. Thus all stated empty-variable and empty-family cases are covered.

title: Supported division over complete parameter coefficients and the flat fibre criterion
statement:
Let $L$ be a field, $A=L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m]]$, $\mathfrak n=(W)$, and $B=A[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]]$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Fix ordered transverse vertices $\alpha_i$, degrees $d_i=|\alpha_i|>0$, their orthant diagram $D$, and first-vertex quotient supports $\Delta_i$ [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. Let $f_i\in B$ and write $\bar f_i\in L[[Z]]$ for reduction modulo $\mathfrak n$. Suppose $\bar f_i$ has order $d_i$ and initial homogeneous form $H_i$, and, for every degree $t$, the indexed family $\{Z^\beta H_i:\beta\in\Delta_i,\ |\beta|+d_i=t\}\amalg\{Z^\gamma:\gamma\notin D,\ |\gamma|=t\}$ is an $L$-basis. Then every $h\in B$ has a unique expression
$$h=\sum_iq_i f_i+r,\qquad \operatorname{supp}_Z q_i\subseteq\Delta_i,\quad\operatorname{supp}_Z r\subseteq\mathbf N^n\setminus D.$$
The coefficients of $q_i,r$ belong to the complete ring $A$; the maps are $A$-linear, continuous for the $(W,Z)$-adic topology, and commute with reduction modulo $(W)$. Let $J=(f_i)\subset B$ and suppose $B/J$ is flat over $A$, meaning tensoring preserves exact sequences [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. If every element of $\bar J=(\bar f_i)\subset L[[Z]]$ is a supported sum $\sum\bar q_i\bar f_i$, then every element of $J$ is a supported sum $\sum q_i f_i$. In particular this holds for every $Z^\beta f_i$. For a continuous local coefficient homomorphism $A\to A'=L'[[W']]$ and the induced homomorphism fixing $Z$, each such whole-series identity is preserved. The empty family is included. No algebraicity of a coefficient in $A$ over a ring of regular parameter functions is part of the assertion.
